findings.title: enableSqlExpressions contains unreachable/dead logic and always returns false
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the inverted logic), then returns false in both branches. The feature-toggle read has no effect and the inverted expression is misleading: a future reader may 'fix' the branch and accidentally re-enable SQL expressions when the flag is *disabled*. If the intent is to hard-disable the feature, the function should simply `return false` (or the QueryTypeSQL case should error unconditionally) with a comment explaining the CVE; the dead flag check should be removed.

findings.title: Misleading error message for disabled SQL expressions
findings.body: Returning "sqlExpressions is not implemented" to users who have the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle enabled is confusing, since the feature previously worked and the toggle still exists and is documented. The message should state that SQL expressions are currently disabled/unavailable so operators don't file bugs about a toggle that silently does nothing.

findings.title: No test asserting SQL expressions are disabled
findings.body: This PR is a security fix that disables a code path leading to RCE/LFI, but adds no test. A regression test asserting that `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returns an error (even with the `sqlExpressions` toggle enabled) and that `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto`/`RunCommands` return errors would prevent an accidental re-enable of the vulnerable path.
